The correct minimum is 11/3, which none of the three solutions gives.

Setting D=(0,0), A=(33,0), B=(33,18), C=(0,130), every ellipse through the four points has the form αx² + (112/33)xy + y² − 33αx − 130y = 0, a one-parameter family. Its quadratic-form matrix has trace α+1 and determinant α − (56/33)². Minimizing (α+1)²/det gives α = 1 + 2(56/33)², with (λ_max/λ_min)^{1/2} + (λ_min/λ_max)^{1/2} = 130/33. Taking the root greater than 1 gives an axis ratio of 121/33 = 11/3 ≈ 3.667.

- Solution 1 has the right family but the wrong optimum (α = 1 + C²/2 instead of 1 + 2(56/33)²), giving (65+√5314)/33 ≈ 4.18.
- Solution 2 reaches a numerical estimate ≈ 3.67, close to 11/3 but not exact, and its final answer is 3.67.
- Solution 3 is incoherent and its final line "535" does not follow from its work.
